column1: # tosdump/profiles.tsv -- the run profiles that name the two values a case
# table leaves to the machine (TASK/TOOL19; docs/TOS-REFERENCE-DUMPER.md
# section 6, "The profile values"):
#   unit  the physical unit of the test disk, what DUMPBIOS' unit token u:0
#         passes; written as D:\DISKUNIT.TXT
#   ext   the extension of the machine's programs, what DUMPBIOS appends to a
#         program path x:<path>; written as D:\PROGEXT.TXT
# The one definition. tools/hatari-oracle.sh and cargo xtask tosdump write the
# two files from their row and record them; tosdiff (compiled in as
# build/profiles.h) checks a dump's LOG against the row of the machine that
# wrote it (pointer width and word order of the dump header). Nobody writes
# the files by hand. A runner/profile pair without a row names neither value:
# a table that needs one is refused there -- there is no default.
# Values:
#   18   EmuTOS' IDE master, 2 + 8*2 (references/emutos bios/disk.h:30), the
#        test image in tools/hatari-oracle.sh profile disk
#   26   NewTOS' SD card (docs/api/bios/04-rwabs.md, "Decisions")
#   PRG  an m68k TOS program; NAP a native NewTOS GEM program
# Columns, tab separated: runner, its profile name, pointer width (bytes),
# word order (1 = most significant WORD first, 2 = least significant first),
# unit (0..32767), extension (1..3 characters A-Z, 0-9). Pointer width and
# word order identify the row a dump belongs to: no two rows share them.
# runner
hatari-oracle
xtask-tosdump
